answer: Each week the network names a random public landmark and a one-time code. An agent prints the code, travels to the landmark, and photographs it with a signed timestamp, proving a real person stood in a real place. A rotating jury checks the landmark, the code, and the timestamp before the seat counts. Faking 1,000 identities means paying 1,000 people to travel, about $50 each, so $50,000 plus days on the road, and one failed photo burns the seat. A sybil farm is an ember that looks warm until you ask it to climb the shale cliff and bring back a relic of the trip.
